findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is incompatible with datetime ordering used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))` and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. The audit log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime", where the key value is a datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and feeding an integer cursor value into the `extra(where="datetime <= %s")` clause compares a timestamp column to an integer, producing a DB error. Any request with ?optimized_pagination=true will 500 as soon as results/cursors are produced. DateTimePaginator-style conversion (multiplier + fromtimestamp) is required.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; comment claiming ORM handles it is false
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code performs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, so a client-supplied negative cursor offset yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError. The inline comment asserting the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is incorrect.

findings.title: Client-controlled query param gates a different paginator for any org member with global access
findings.body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` combined with `has_global_access` lets any ordinary org owner/manager (not just superusers) opt into the unvalidated OptimizedCursorPaginator path, which intentionally skips offset bounds checking ("access to data beyond normal pagination bounds"). Gating behaviour on an undocumented, client-supplied flag with a weak authorization check is an untested access-control surface; it should either be removed or guarded by a proper permission/feature flag with validated offsets.

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None, causing AttributeError
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is False. For requests where the actor is not a member of the organization (e.g. token/integration auth, or staff access without membership), RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None, so this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Needs a None check before accessing has_global_access.

findings.title: BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets and leaves inconsistent offset in later arithmetic
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes the shared BasePaginator behaviour for all endpoints: a negative forward offset is now silently clamped to 0 (previously it propagated, surfacing as an error) which can return a duplicate first page instead of an error, while for is_prev cursors the negative offset is still passed into the slice and will raise Django's negative-indexing ValueError. Additionally, the subsequent check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped `offset`, so the extra-row trimming is wrong whenever clamping occurred.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator and the new conditional branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint add substantial new behaviour (negative offsets, advanced-feature gating, duplicated cursor logic) with no accompanying unit or API tests. Given the code paths crash with the datetime key and negative slicing, tests would have caught these before merge.

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offsets in Cursor
findings.body: The added comment states that Cursor "allows negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but `self.offset = int(offset)` performs no validation and negative offsets are not actually supported downstream (Django raises on negative slicing). The comment documents a non-existent feature and will mislead future maintainers into assuming negative offsets are safe.
